sources.entry: ChronoFrame - Personal gallery application with online photo management, supporting Live/Motion Photos, and explore map. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: ChronoFrame is a self-hosted photo gallery that extracts EXIF data, generates previews, identifies shooting locations, and supports Live Photos and an explore map.
summary.what_it_does: Users upload photos, and the app extracts EXIF metadata, creates previews, and identifies shooting locations via reverse geocoding. Visitors can browse by time, album, or map, zoom into large images with WebGL tiled rendering, and play Live Photos. Albums can be reordered, hidden, or protected with passwords. The dashboard handles batch uploads, metadata and rating edits, batch downloads, reindexing, and a task queue with live logs. Storage can be local files, S3-compatible services, or OpenList, with CDN URLs managed in the dashboard. A browser-based setup wizard creates the administrator and configures storage.
use_cases: play Apple Live Photos on a website
store photos in S3-compatible object storage
how_to_run: Create docker-compose.yml with the ghcr.io/hoshinosuzumi/chronoframe:latest image, port 3000:3000, and ./data:/app/data volume
Or run directly: docker run -d --name chronoframe --restart unless-stopped -p 3000:3000 -v "$(pwd)/data:/app/data" ghcr.io/hoshinosuzumi/chronoframe:latest
Open the app in a browser and complete the setup wizard; for local storage enter /app/data/storage
Development: corepack enable, then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm dev (Node.js 22, pnpm 10.34.6)
notable: Automatic pairing of Apple Live/Motion Photo image and video files by shared filename
WebGL zoom and tiled rendering for large images
Storage backends include local files, S3-compatible services, and OpenList with CDN URL support
Browser-based setup wizard for admin and storage configuration
Explore map with reverse geocoding and selectable place-name language
caveats: Album passwords only control access within ChronoFrame; public S3, OpenList, or CDN URLs must be secured in those services
Public deployments should use HTTPS, which requires a proxy setup not covered in the README
Map features need a MapLibre or Mapbox token configured later
